method: In-session LLM analysis (Claude) of web news + Fed/EIA RSS; same schema as src/agent.py

scan.policy_summary: Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep 2026 (first hike since 2023, unanimous); median dot shows one more hike to ~4.1% by end-2026, no cuts in 2027. Inflation (CPI 3.4% y/y Aug, core 2.4%) is energy-led, while labor is softening (Sep payrolls +29k, July revised negative, wage growth 3.0%, slowest since 2021): a stagflationary policy bind.

shocks.event: US-Iran war (since Feb 2026) and Strait of Hormuz disruption; US blockade of Iranian ports, third carrier deployed, tanker rates ~43x January
shocks.first_order: Energy (XLE) up via oil risk premium (WTI ~$93-96, Brent >$100); airlines/transports in Industrials down on fuel cost
shocks.second_order: Gasoline $4.35/gal squeezes discretionary wallets (XLY down); higher inflation expectations push yields up, hurting rate-sensitive XLU/XLRE; defense names in XLI benefit

shocks.event: Global bond selloff: 10Y Treasury hit 5.34% (highest since 2002), +110bp YTD on Fed hikes, deficits and supply
shocks.first_order: Bond proxies down: Utilities (XLU), Real Estate (XLRE), Staples (XLP); long-duration growth multiples at risk
shocks.second_order: 30Y mortgage 7.44% (from 6.34% a year ago) freezes housing: homebuilders/home improvement (XLY), building materials (XLB) weaken; regional banks face deposit-cost pressure on NIM

shocks.event: Refined-product squeeze: Russia diesel export ban after Ukrainian refinery strikes; China halts October fuel exports
shocks.first_order: Refiners and integrated oils (XLE) gain on crack spreads
shocks.second_order: Diesel costs hit trucking, chemicals feedstock (XLB margins) and farm inputs; feeds PPI (+9.9% y/y), keeps Fed hawkish

shocks.event: Consumer sentiment at/near record lows (UMich ~52); 76% of drivers cutting other spending due to gas prices
shocks.first_order: Consumer Discretionary (XLY) earnings risk: dining, travel, entertainment
shocks.second_order: Trade-down benefits discount retailers within XLP; credit-card delinquencies a watch item for XLF

shocks.event: AI capex boom: top hyperscalers ~$600-690bn capex in 2026; US utilities planning ~$1.4tn through 2030; power is the binding constraint
shocks.first_order: Semis/hardware (XLK) earnings strong; XLK the only sector up in September (+5%)
shocks.second_order: Grid/electrical equipment (XLI), copper (XLB) and gas generation benefit; regulated utilities need heavy capex financed at 5%+ yields, so negative FCF caps equity upside despite demand

shocks.event: Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs (Feb 2026); Section 232/301 tariffs remain; potential refunds of >$200bn to importers
shocks.first_order: Lower import costs/refunds support retailers and autos (XLY) at the margin
shocks.second_order: Refunds widen the deficit, adding to Treasury supply pressure; steel/aluminum 232 tariffs still protect domestic Materials

shocks.event: Most-Favored-Nation drug pricing deals with 17 large pharma firms; GLP-1 price cuts via TrumpRx
shocks.first_order: Branded pharma (XLV) pricing headwind, partly priced in; volume uplift for GLP-1 makers
shocks.second_order: GLP-1 adoption weighs on snack/beverage volumes (XLP) and supports medtech/insurers' cost trends

Only sector up in September (+5%); AI capex intact, but 5%+ yields threaten multiples
Defensive growth in a slowing economy; MFN pricing a known overhang
Steeper curve helps, but money-center NIM compressed and deposit costs rising; earnings 13-15 Oct are a catalyst
Grid/defense tailwinds vs. airlines and transports hit by fuel
Worst sector in September (-7.6%); housing freeze and diesel feedstock costs
Gas prices and record-low sentiment; YTD -8.7%, worst sector
Rate-sensitive; pressured by bond selloff despite AI power demand
Defensive, but bond-proxy and GLP-1 volume headwinds

flags_vs_model: XLK long conflicts with the macro layer (rising rates, stagflation quadrant): news flow supports the technical/fundamental case; size smaller or pair with a rate hedge
XLU short conflicts with the AI power-demand secular theme: keep, since rates dominate near-term, but revisit if 10Y falls back below ~4.75%
Materials (XLB) news flow is the weakest, but the model ranks it neutral (-0.05): a candidate replacement short if RSI/relative strength deteriorate further
Ceasefire risk: a US-Iran deal would unwind the energy premium quickly; XLE long needs a stop (e.g. WTI < $80 or relative strength below 200d)

rss_headlines.title: Crude oil prices and refinery margins generally increased throughout the third quarter
rss_headlines.summary: Petroleum markets in the third quarter of 2026 (3Q26) were characterized by increasing prices for crude oil and petroleum products amid persistent conflict in the Middle East.

rss_headlines.title: U.S. natural gas production reached a record high in July 2026
rss_headlines.summary: U.S. natural gas production hit an all-time high in July 2026, driven primarily by increased output in the Permian Basin, according to our latest Natural Gas Monthly.

rss_headlines.summary: U.S. propane exports increased to 2 million barrels per day (b/d) in the first half of 2026, 11% more than during the same period in 2025. Increased U.S. propane production and changing trade flows, particularly increased exports to India and other countries in South Asia, drove propane exports to a record high of 2.1 million (b/d) in April 2026. rss_headlines.summary: We estimate light-duty electric vehicles in the United States consumed 8% more electricity during the first six months of 2026 than in the last half of 2025 (2H25) in our Monthly Energy Review, down from the 13-24% growth seen in six-month periods in recent years. rss_headlines.title: Henry Hub natural gas prices this summer were 6% lower than last summer
rss_headlines.summary: The Henry Hub natural gas spot price averaged $2.93 per million British thermal units from June through August, 6% less than the same period last year. Prices were lower this summer despite exceptionally hot weather that increased electricity demand for air conditioning. Natural gas-fired power plants often help meet higher demand during such periods.

rss_headlines.title: Public companies produce most U.S. crude oil and natural gas
rss_headlines.summary: Publicly traded companies represent a tiny share of the total number of companies producing crude oil and natural gas in the United States, but they make up a large share of U.S. production. In 2025, publicly traded companies accounted for just 2% of about 12,000 oil and natural gas producers but produced 68% of the crude oil and natural gas in the Lower 48 states.

rss_headlines.title: What goes into diesel prices?
rss_headlines.summary: The price of distillate fuel oil, often sold as diesel, is driven by the price of crude oil, retail margins, distribution costs, taxes, and crack spreads, the indicator we use for refining margins. Tight global supplies of distillate fuel oil and elevated crude oil prices have driven prices higher in recent months.

rss_headlines.title: Corpus Christi LNG expansion makes facility the second-largest in the United States
rss_headlines.summary: On August 28, 2026, Cheniere Energy, Inc., completed its Corpus Christi Liquefaction Stage 3 Project (CCL Stage 3) in Texas, taking custody and control of the seventh and last liquefied natural gas (LNG) train in the project.

rss_headlines.title: United States on track for record crude oil production in 2026
rss_headlines.summary: We forecast U.S. crude oil production will average 13.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in 2026, surpassing the previous record of 13.7 million b/d set in 2025, in our latest Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO).

rss_headlines.title: New England natural gas prices have been trading near record discounts to Henry Hub
rss_headlines.summary: Low-cost Appalachian and Canadian natural gas supplies coupled with lower-than-usual regional consumption have pushed down natural gas prices at a major New England pricing hub in recent months to trade at a discount to the widely cited U.S. benchmark, Henry Hub.

rss_headlines.title: Elevated crack spreads and crude oil prices contribute to higher prices at the pump
rss_headlines.summary: What are crack spreads and why are they elevated? Crack spreads are indicators of the profitability of refining crude oil into petroleum products such as gasoline and diesel. One common crack spread is calculated by subtracting the spot market price of a gallon of crude oil from the wholesale price of a gallon of refined product. rss_headlines.title: Weekly average load in ERCOT continues near record high
rss_headlines.summary: Sustained high temperatures have contributed to persistently high electricity demand in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), the regional transmission organization for most of the state.
